title: Reading Simple Floor Plans
description: Learn to identify basic symbols and rooms on a residential floor plan.
passageText: An architect draws a floor plan to show the layout of a house. The plan shows rooms, doors, and walls. Each room has a label. The living room is usually large. The kitchen is near the dining area. Bedrooms are placed for privacy. Doors are shown as gaps in walls. Windows are thin lines on exterior walls. The scale helps builders measure real dimensions from the drawing.

title: Building Materials Overview
description: Identify common materials used in residential construction.
passageText: Architects choose materials based on strength, cost, and appearance. Concrete is strong under compression and is used for foundations and columns. Steel reinforcement adds tensile strength to concrete structures. Brick is common for walls because it is durable and fire-resistant. Timber is used for roofs and floors in many homes. Glass allows natural light into buildings while protecting from weather. Insulation materials reduce heat loss and improve energy efficiency.

title: Structural Systems in Buildings
description: Understand how loads travel through a building frame.
passageText: A building's structural system transfers loads safely to the ground. Vertical loads include the weight of the structure itself, occupants, and furniture. Lateral loads come from wind and earthquakes. In a frame structure, beams carry floor loads to columns, which transfer them to the foundation. Shear walls resist horizontal forces. The foundation spreads the load across the soil. Architects and structural engineers collaborate to select the appropriate system for each project.

title: Sustainable Design Principles
description: Explore energy-efficient strategies in modern architecture.
passageText: Sustainable architecture minimizes environmental impact while maximizing occupant comfort. Passive design strategies use natural sunlight and ventilation to reduce energy consumption. High-performance glazing limits heat gain in summer and heat loss in winter. Green roofs provide insulation and reduce stormwater runoff. Solar panels generate renewable electricity on site. Rainwater harvesting systems collect water for irrigation and non-potable uses. Life-cycle assessment evaluates the environmental impact of materials from extraction to disposal.

title: Urban Planning Fundamentals
description: Understand how cities are organized and zoned for different uses.
passageText: Urban planning shapes the physical and functional organization of cities. Zoning regulations separate residential, commercial, and industrial areas to minimize conflicts. Mixed-use developments combine housing, retail, and offices in a single district to reduce commuting distances. Transit-oriented development clusters housing and services around public transport hubs. Planners analyze population density, infrastructure capacity, and environmental constraints to guide growth. Public participation ensures that community needs influence planning decisions.
